options.why_wrong: The present simple active does not form a passive, and 'yesterday' needs a past form.
This is an active sentence with the object 'it', so it does not describe the message being the receiver of the action.
The present perfect continuous does not fit with the finished time 'yesterday', and it is not passive.

explanation: The passive uses was or were plus the past participle when the subject receives the action. Speakers of Spanish often use the active form here because Spanish passive constructions are used less often in everyday speech.
